verses.1: A song of ascents. LORD, remember David and all his anxious care;
verses.2: How he swore an oath to the LORD, vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob:
verses.3: "I will not enter the house where I live, nor lie on the couch where I sleep;
verses.4: I will give my eyes no sleep, my eyelids no rest,
verses.5: Till I find a home for the LORD, a dwelling for the Mighty One of Jacob."
verses.6: "We have heard of it in Ephrathah; we have found it in the fields of Jaar.
verses.7: Let us enter God's dwelling; let us worship at God's footstool."
verses.8: "Arise, LORD, come to your resting place, you and your majestic ark.
verses.9: Your priests will be clothed with justice; your faithful will shout for joy."
verses.10: For the sake of David your servant, do not reject your anointed.
verses.11: The LORD swore an oath to David, a pledge never to be broken: "Your own offspring I will set upon your throne.
verses.12: If your sons observe my covenant, the laws I shall teach them, Their sons, in turn, shall sit forever on your throne."
verses.13: Yes, the LORD has chosen Zion, desired it for a dwelling:
verses.14: "This is my resting place forever; here I will dwell, for I desire it.
verses.15: I will bless Zion with meat; its poor I will fill with bread.
verses.16: I will clothe its priests with blessing; its faithful shall shout for joy.
verses.17: There I will make a horn sprout for David's line; I will set a lamp for my anointed.
verses.18: His foes I will clothe with shame, but on him my crown shall gleam."

notes.text: All his anxious care: to build the temple. Cf 2 Sam 7:1-17 and 1 Kings 8:17.
Mighty One of Jacob: one of the titles of Israel's God. Cf Genesis 49:24; Isaiah 49:26; 60:16.

Ephrathah: the homeland of David. Cf Ruth 4:11. The fields of Jaar: poetic for Kiriath-jearim, a town west of Jerusalem, where the ark remained for several generations. Cf 1 Sam 7:1-2; 2 Sam 6:2; 1 Chron 13:5-6.

A horn sprout for David's line: the image of the horn, a symbol of strength, is combined with that of a "sprout," a term used for the Davidic descendant (cf Jeremiah 23:5; 33:15; Zechariah 3:8; 6:12). Early Christians referred the latter designation to Christ as son of David (Luke 1:69).
